Abbasidsand the non-Arabs
The main feature of Abbasid administration was giving important positions to mawalis or
the non-Arabs. After declaring Baghdad as their capital, the Abbasid caliphs established
the office of thevizier as themost powerful authority after caliph.Mawali viziers were
appointed to this position. Khalid Barmaki of the Persian origin was appointed as head of

AbbasidAchievements intheFieldof Science
The greatest contribution of Abbasid to Islamic civilization was in thefields of science.
Abbasid caliphs gave great importance to scientists. Baghdad, the capital of the Abbasid
Empire,becamecentreof intellectualandscientificlearning.Ahouseof wisdomwiththe
name Bayt al-Hikmah was established bythe Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid and further
flourished by Mamun al Rashid.This was a great evidence of support of Abbasids for
science.Within few decades Baghdad became a centre of learning.Many educational
institutions, hospitals, masjids, and libraries made Baghdad'an attraction for students
from different parts of the world.
